theory.intro: The height, the horizontal distance and the line of sight form a right-angled triangle. Mark the angle of elevation or depression from the horizontal, then use the usual trigonometric ratios.
facts: The angle of **elevation** is measured up from the horizontal at the observer; the angle of **depression** is measured down from it.
Mark that equal angle inside the triangle before choosing a ratio.
An angle measured from a vertical wall is not an angle of depression; subtract it from $90^{\circ}$ first.
Keep the full calculator value through the working and round only on the last line, to the accuracy the question asks for.
steps: Draw a diagram and mark the horizontal.
Mark the angle of elevation or depression inside the triangle.

workedExamples.question_text: From a point on level ground $20$ m from the base of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of its top is $30^{\circ}$. Find the height of the tower, correct to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(4,2.309)--cycle;\draw (3.75,0)--(3.75,0.25)--(4,0.25);\draw (0.7,0) arc (0:30:0.7);\path (1,0.25) node {$30^{\circ}$} (2,-0.35) node {$20\text{ m}\ (A)$} (4.75,1.15) node {$h\ (O)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
The height is opposite the angle; the horizontal distance is adjacent.
$\begin{aligned}\tan 30^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{20}\\h&=20\tan 30^{\circ}\\h&\approx11.55\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A boat is observed from the top of a vertical cliff $72$ m above sea level at an angle of depression of $45^{\circ}$. Find its horizontal distance from the base of the cliff, to the nearest metre.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,3)--(0,0)--(3,0)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (0,3)--(3.8,3);\draw (0,0.25)--(0.25,0.25)--(0.25,0);\draw (0.7,3) arc (0:-45:0.7);\draw (2.3,0) arc (180:135:0.7);\path (1.15,2.75) node {$45^{\circ}$} (2.05,0.4) node {$45^{\circ}$} (-0.65,1.5) node {$72\text{ m}\ (O)$} (1.5,-0.35) node {$d\ (A)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
The angle of elevation from the boat is also $45^{\circ}$ because alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
$\begin{aligned}\tan45^{\circ}&=\frac{72}{d}\\d\tan45^{\circ}&=72\\d&=\frac{72}{\tan45^{\circ}}\\d&=72\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A plane is $24$ m above level ground and $32$ m horizontally from an observer on the ground. Find its angle of elevation, correct to $2$ decimal places. Hence state the angle of depression of the observer from the plane.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(4,3)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (4,3)--(-0.5,3);\draw (3.75,0)--(3.75,0.25)--(4,0.25);\draw (0.7,0) arc (0:36.87:0.7);\draw (3.3,3) arc (180:216.87:0.7);\path (1,0.3) node {$\theta$} (3,2.7) node {$\theta$} (2,-0.35) node {$32\text{ m}\ (A)$} (4.75,1.5) node {$24\text{ m}\ (O)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{24}{32}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24}{32}\right)\\\theta&\approx36.87^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
The angle of depression is also $36.87^{\circ}$ because alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.

workedExamples.question_text: A kite is $30$ m above its anchor point on level ground. Its straight, fully extended string is $50$ m long. Find the angle of elevation of the kite from the anchor point, to the nearest degree.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(4,3)--cycle;\draw (3.75,0)--(3.75,0.25)--(4,0.25);\draw (0.7,0) arc (0:36.87:0.7);\path (1,0.3) node {$\theta$} (4.75,1.5) node {$30\text{ m}\ (O)$} (2,1.85) node[above,sloped,rotate=36.87] {$50\text{ m}\ (H)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\sin\theta&=\frac{30}{50}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{30}{50}\right)\\\theta&\approx37^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: An owl is $24$ m above level ground. It sees a mouse on the ground at an angle of depression of $30^{\circ}$. How far must it fly in a straight line to reach the mouse? Answer correct to $1$ decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,2.309)--(0,0)--(4,0)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (0,2.309)--(4.8,2.309);\draw (0,0.25)--(0.25,0.25)--(0.25,0);\draw (0.7,2.309) arc (0:-30:0.7);\draw (3.3,0) arc (180:150:0.7);\path (1.1,2.05) node {$30^{\circ}$} (2.95,0.3) node {$30^{\circ}$} (-0.7,1.15) node {$24\text{ m}\ (O)$} (2,1.5) node {$L\ (H)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
The angle of elevation from the mouse is also $30^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{24}{L}\\L\sin30^{\circ}&=24\\L&=\frac{24}{\sin30^{\circ}}\\L&=48.0\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: An observer stands $18$ m from the base of a vertical tree on level ground. The angle of elevation of its top is $45^{\circ}$, measured from an eye height of $1.7$ m. Find the height of the tree, correct to $1$ decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,0)--(3,0)--(3,3.283);\draw (0,0)--(0,0.283);\draw[dashed] (0,0.283)--(3,0.283);\draw (0,0.283)--(3,3.283);\draw (2.75,0.283)--(2.75,0.533)--(3,0.533);\draw (0.6,0.283) arc (0:45:0.6);\path (0.95,0.58) node {$45^{\circ}$} (-0.7,0.14) node {$1.7\text{ m}$} (1.5,-0.35) node {$18\text{ m}\ (A)$} (3.65,1.8) node {$x\ (O)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\tan45^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{18}\\x&=18\tan45^{\circ}\\x&=18\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
Add the eye height to the height above eye level.
$\begin{aligned}h&=18+1.7\\h&=19.7\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A cable joins the top of a $3$ m high shed to the top of a $9$ m pole. Their horizontal separation is $8$ m. Find the angle of elevation of the pole top from the shed top, correct to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,0)--(4,0);\draw (0,0)--(0,1.5);\draw (4,0)--(4,4.5);\draw[dashed] (0,1.5)--(4,1.5);\draw (0,1.5)--(4,4.5);\draw (3.75,1.5)--(3.75,1.75)--(4,1.75);\draw (0.7,1.5) arc (0:36.87:0.7);\path (1,1.8) node {$\theta$} (-0.5,0.75) node {$3\text{ m}$} (4.55,0.75) node {$3\text{ m}$} (4.75,3) node {$6\text{ m}\ (O)$} (2,1.15) node {$8\text{ m}\ (A)$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
The vertical difference is $9-3=6$ m.
$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{6}{8}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{8}\right)\\\theta&\approx36.87^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: From the top of a $60$ m vertical cliff, two boats on the same side of the cliff and in line with its base have angles of depression of $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$. Find the distance between them, to the nearest metre.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,2.4)--(0,0)--(4.157,0);\draw (0,2.4)--(2.4,0);\draw (0,2.4)--(4.157,0);\draw[dashed] (0,2.4)--(4.9,2.4);\draw (0,0.25)--(0.25,0.25)--(0.25,0);\draw (1.2,2.4) arc (0:-30:1.2);\draw (0.55,2.4) arc (0:-45:0.55);\path (1.65,2.05) node {$30^{\circ}$} (0.8,1.95) node {$45^{\circ}$} (-0.65,1.2) node {$60\text{ m}$} (2.4,-0.3) node {$B_2$} (4.157,-0.3) node {$B_1$};\draw[<->] (0,-0.7)--(2.4,-0.7);\draw[<->] (0,-1.15)--(4.157,-1.15);\path (1.2,-0.9) node {$d_2$} (2.08,-1.35) node {$d_1$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
The corresponding angles of elevation are $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{60}{d_1}\\d_1&=\frac{60}{\tan30^{\circ}}\\d_1&=103.9230\ldots\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\tan45^{\circ}&=\frac{60}{d_2}\\d_2&=\frac{60}{\tan45^{\circ}}\\d_2&=60\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
Subtract the distances from the cliff base, retaining the full calculator value.
$\begin{aligned}B_1B_2&=\frac{60}{\tan30^{\circ}}-60\\B_1B_2&\approx44\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: From a point on level ground $100$ m from the base of a building, the angles of elevation of the bottom and top of a vertical flagpole on its roof are $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$. Find the flagpole height, correct to $1$ decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,0)--(4,0)--(4,4);\draw (0,0)--(4,2.309);\draw (0,0)--(4,4);\draw (3.75,0)--(3.75,0.25)--(4,0.25);\draw (0.65,0) arc (0:30:0.65);\draw (1.4,0) arc (0:45:1.4);\path (1,0.22) node {$30^{\circ}$} (1.65,0.8) node {$45^{\circ}$} (2,-0.35) node {$100\text{ m}$} (4.3,2.309) node {$A$} (4.3,4) node {$B$};\draw[<->] (4.8,0)--(4.8,2.309);\draw[<->] (5.6,0)--(5.6,4);\path (5.05,1.15) node {$h_1$} (5.85,2) node {$h_2$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{h_1}{100}\\h_1&=100\tan30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\tan45^{\circ}&=\frac{h_2}{100}\\h_2&=100\tan45^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Subtract the height of the bottom from the height of the top.
$\begin{aligned}AB&=h_2-h_1\\AB&=100\tan45^{\circ}-100\tan30^{\circ}\\AB&\approx42.3\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A plane at an altitude of $800$ m begins a straight climb at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. A mountain peak $1300$ m high is $1000$ m ahead horizontally. Will the plane clear the peak, and by how much? Answer to the nearest metre.
workedExamples.solution_text:
[tikz]\begin{tikzpicture}[draw=black,text=black,every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont}]\draw (0,0)--(4,0);\draw[dashed] (0,0)--(0,3.2);\draw[dashed] (0,3.2)--(4,3.2);\draw (0,3.2)--(4,5.509);\draw[dashed] (4,0)--(4,5.509);\draw (3.75,3.2)--(3.75,3.45)--(4,3.45);\draw (0.7,3.2) arc (0:30:0.7);\path (1.05,3.45) node {$30^{\circ}$} (2,-0.35) node {$1000\text{ m}\ (A)$} (-0.6,1.6) node {$800\text{ m}$} (4.65,4.35) node {$x\ (O)$};\draw (3,0)--(4,5.2)--(5,0);\path (5.05,2.6) node {$1300\text{ m}$};\end{tikzpicture}[/tikz]
$\begin{aligned}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{1000}\\x&=1000\tan30^{\circ}\\x&=577.3502\ldots\text{ m}\end{aligned}$
The altitude at the peak is $800+1000\tan30^{\circ}=1377.3502\ldots$ m, so the plane clears it.
$\begin{aligned}c&=800+1000\tan30^{\circ}-1300\\c&\approx77\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (A) at (0,1.62);\coordinate (C) at (0,0);\coordinate (Bp) at (2.402,0);\coordinate (Hz) at (3.252,1.62);\draw[dashed] (A)--(Hz);\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,left] {$18\text{ m}$};\draw (C)--(Bp);\draw (A)--(Bp) node[midway,above right] {$L$};\coordinate (rqa) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(A)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(Bp)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(C)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$34^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=Bp--A--Hz};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
From a window $18$ m above the ground in an office building, the angle of depression of a car is $34^{\circ}$.
Find the line-of-sight distance $L$ from the window to the car, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
The angle of elevation of the window from the car is also $34^{\circ}$, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\sin 34^{\circ}=\dfrac{18}{L}$
$L\sin 34^{\circ}=18$
$L=\dfrac{18}{\sin 34^{\circ}}$
$\approx 32.2\text{ m}$

[/tikz]
The lamp of a lighthouse is $52$ m above sea level.
The line-of-sight distance from the lamp to a ship is $260$ m. Find the angle of depression $\theta$ of the ship from the lamp, to the nearest degree.
development.solution_text:
The angle of elevation of the lamp from the ship equals the angle of depression, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{52}{260}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{52}{260}\right)$
$\approx 12^{\circ}$

A plane is flying at an altitude of $2400$ m. The pilot sees the base of a control tower at ground level, a horizontal distance of $9500$ m ahead.
Find the angle of depression $\theta$ of the base of the tower from the plane, to the nearest degree.
development.solution_text:
The angle of elevation of the plane from the base of the tower equals the angle of depression, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{2400}{9500}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2400}{9500}\right)$
$\approx 14^{\circ}$

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (G) at (0,0);\coordinate (P) at (0,2.59);\coordinate (Mb) at (3.64,0);\coordinate (K) at (3.64,3.43);\coordinate (Hh) at (1.3,2.59);\coordinate (E) at (2.002,3.24);\draw (G)--(Mb) node[midway,below] {$2600\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (G)--(P) node[midway,left] {$1850\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (Mb)--(K) node[midway,right] {$2450\text{ m}$};\draw (2.64,0)--(K)--(4.64,0);\draw (Mb)--(4.64,0);\draw[dashed] (P)--(Hh);\draw[-{Stealth}] (P)--(E);\pic[draw,"$18^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=Hh--P--E};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A plane flying at an altitude of $1850$ m begins to climb at $18^{\circ}$ to the horizontal when the pilot sees a mountain peak $2450$ m high, $2600$ m away horizontally.
Will the plane clear the peak, and by how much?
Answer to the nearest metre.
mastery.solution_text:
$\tan 18^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{2600}$
$x=2600\tan 18^{\circ}$
$=844.79\ldots$
The plane is then at $1850+844.79\ldots=2694.79\ldots$ m, which is above the $2450$ m peak, so it clears it.
$2694.79\ldots-2450\approx 245\text{ m}$
